components.title: Accordion
components.description: Accordion coordinates named, in-flow disclosure sections with single or multiple selection, accessible keyboard navigation, and finished surfaces.

components.title: Alert Dialog
components.description: AlertDialog interrupts the current workflow for a brief, important decision that requires an explicit response. Atom owns alert-dialog semantics, modal state, focus, portals, isolation, stacking, presence, and scroll containment; Brick supplies the finished visual anatomy.

components.title: App Bar
components.description: AppBar is a top surface and one-row alignment structure built on Atom AppBar.

components.title: Appearance
components.description: Appearance applies an explicit light, dark, or inherited semantic-token scope to one native or existing Brick host. It adds no paint, spacing, state, persistence, or required client provider.

components.title: Aspect Ratio
components.description: Aspect Ratio reserves stable width-to-height geometry for authored media, embeds, placeholders, and layout content. It controls the box and optional frame only; children retain their own semantics, sizing, and behavior.

components.title: Avatar
components.description: Avatar presents an image or fallback identity in a finished Brick frame.

components.title: Badge
components.description: Badge is a compact passive label for categories, status, or short metadata.

components.title: Bleed
components.description: Bleed lets authored content extend beyond the inset of its immediate container using responsive, theme-aware logical spacing.

components.title: Bottom Navigation
components.description: Bottom Navigation presents three to five stable, equal-priority top-level destinations in a compact navigation surface.

components.title: Breadcrumb
components.description: Breadcrumb is Brick's finished hierarchy trail. It styles Atom's named navigation landmark, ordered list, native ancestor links, current page, decorative separators, and composable Ellipsis without owning route data.

components.title: Button
components.description: Button presents a finished action or emphasized native link. Brick owns its visual recipes and styling; the public Atom Button owns semantics, interaction, form behavior, unavailable/loading behavior, and composition.

components.title: Card
components.description: Card is a static compound surface for grouping information and related actions about one subject.

components.title: Carousel
components.description: Carousel presents one peer slide at a time with native touch scrolling and optional finished controls.

components.title: Checkbox
components.description: Checkbox is a styled binary or mixed-state form choice built on Atom Checkbox.

components.title: Checkbox Group
components.description: CheckboxGroup coordinates related Checkbox-style items, optional item text, and an aggregate parent control.

components.title: Chip
components.description: Chip presents one compact authored or selected value with an optional, explicitly named remove action. It does not replace Badge, Button, Toggle, Link, or a future token-entry collection.

components.title: Code
components.description: Code renders short inline technical text with native `code` semantics and finished Brick recipes.

components.title: Code Block
components.description: Code Block presents structured multi-line source with native scrolling, explicit language metadata, and truthful Atom-backed copy behavior.

components.title: Collapsible
components.description: Collapsible reveals one independent in-flow content region from a linked button trigger.

components.title: Color Picker
components.description: Color Picker provides a finished Atom-backed control for editing, choosing, and submitting one opaque hexadecimal color. It supports editable text, the browser-native chooser, named presets, and optional floating content without application CSS.

components.title: Color Swatch
components.description: Color Swatch provides a finished passive preview for one CSS color or a compact mix of colors. Its checkerboard reveals alpha without requiring application CSS.

components.title: Combobox
components.description: Combobox is Brick's finished searchable single-value choice control. Atom owns filtering, keyboard focus, selection, open state, collision-aware positioning, dismissal, ARIA, and optional free text; Brick owns its visual system.

components.title: Container
components.description: Container creates a centered, fluid content boundary with a closed maximum measure and logical inline gutters. It renders one native element and adds no paint, vertical spacing, child layout, role, or behavior.

components.title: Context Menu
components.description: Context Menu provides commands for a pointer or touch context region through Atom-owned semantics and behavior.

components.title: Data Grid
components.description: Data Grid presents tabular data with Atom-owned cell navigation, row selection, active-cell semantics, and sortable-header activation. Brick supplies the finished visual recipes; applications own data transforms and surrounding controls.

components.title: Data List
components.description: Data List presents repeated term/value metadata with native description-list semantics and responsive Brick recipes.

components.title: Dialog
components.description: Dialog presents a focused modal task or information surface above the current page. Atom owns modal state, focus, dismissal, portals, background isolation, scroll containment, and presence; Brick supplies the finished visual anatomy.

components.title: Divider
components.description: Divider draws a low-emphasis structural line between adjacent content groups. It uses Atom for decorative or semantic separator behavior and adds finished line, inset, label, and appearance recipes.

components.title: Drawer
components.description: Drawer is a modal task surface that enters from a logical or physical edge.

components.title: Dropdown Menu
components.description: Dropdown Menu provides button-triggered commands, persistent choices, and nested actions through Atom-owned semantics and behavior.

components.title: Feed
components.description: Feed presents a styled dynamic stream of rich, focusable articles. Atom owns Feed semantics, positions, busy state, focus, and keyboard movement; Brick owns article separation, density, surfaces, focus paint, and customization hooks.

components.title: Field
components.description: Field coordinates one control’s label, description, error, and required state.

components.title: Fieldset
components.description: Fieldset coordinates a related control group with a legend, description, and group error.

components.title: File Upload
components.description: File Upload is Brick's styled file picker, drop target, and removable selected-file list, backed directly by Atom. It works alone or as the sole control in one `Field`; file transfer, upload progress, persistence, and server policy remain application concerns.

components.title: Form
components.description: Form is Brick’s styled form boundary over Atom’s native form behavior.

components.title: Frame
components.description: Frame owns responsive logical size constraints for one local element. It does not own paint, spacing, child layout, parent participation, aspect ratio, overflow, semantics, or behavior.

components.title: Grid
components.description: Grid is Brick's two-dimensional layout primitive. `Grid.Root` creates exact equal columns or intrinsic responsive columns. Optional `Grid.Item` adds deliberate spans, line placement, and self-alignment; ordinary children remain valid grid items without wrappers.

components.title: Group
components.description: Group creates a compact inline visual cluster and can attach direct children without changing their semantics or keyboard behavior.

components.title: Hide
components.description: Hide keeps content mounted while removing it from visual layout from one fixed viewport breakpoint. It is CSS layout, not conditional React rendering. When visible, its host is layout-transparent so parent flex and grid spacing continue to apply directly to its children.

components.title: Hover Card
components.description: HoverCard shows nonessential preview information from a link-like trigger.

components.title: Icon
components.description: Icon gives one consumer-supplied SVG a consistent Brick size, semantic color, alignment, direction, and accessibility mode. Brick supplies no icon catalog or string registry.

components.title: Icon Button
components.description: IconButton presents one named icon-only action or a button-styled native link with finished Brick geometry and recipes over public Atom Button behavior.

components.title: Image
components.description: Image presents ordinary raster or vector media with authored alternative text, deterministic loading/fallback anatomy, fit and focal-position recipes, stable aspect ratio, and finished framing. Atom owns source lifecycle; Brick owns paint.

components.title: Input
components.description: Input is a finished single-line text-entry control built on Atom Input. Atom owns native input behavior, value state, validation, reset, Field relationships, Clear behavior, and the input ref; Brick owns the visual wrapper, recipes, geometry, adornment layout, and static CSS.

components.title: Link
components.description: Link is Brick's finished typographic navigation component. It styles the server-safe Atom Link primitive while preserving one real native anchor, browser navigation behavior, native attributes, and router composition.

components.title: Link Box
components.description: Link Box expands one real Brick Link across a containing region while keeping secondary controls outside that anchor. It fits product cards, property listings, articles, and result rows with one primary destination.

components.title: List
components.description: List presents related static content through native unordered or ordered list semantics, finished markers and boundaries, and optional structured row anatomy. Atom owns list semantics; Brick owns visual presentation.

components.title: Menubar
components.description: Menubar provides persistent desktop-style command categories through Atom-owned semantics and behavior.

components.title: Multi Select
components.description: MultiSelect is Brick's styled multiple-value choice control. It is built directly on Atom MultiSelect 0.10.1: Atom owns the value array, open state, option registration, keyboard/typeahead, focus, dismissal, positioning, ARIA, native form participation, validation, and reset. Brick owns the complete visual system and default decorative artwork.

components.title: Nav List
components.description: Nav List renders finished native navigation lists, current destinations, and optional grouped disclosure sections on Atom NavList behavior.

components.title: Navigation Menu
components.description: Navigation Menu provides site destinations with optional rich link panels through Atom-owned semantics and behavior.

components.title: Notification Badge
components.description: NotificationBadge overlays a visual count or dot on exactly one child.

components.title: Number Input
components.description: Number Input is a finished numeric entry control backed by Atom Number Input. Atom owns numeric value, parsing, formatting, bounds, stepping, validation, and form behavior; Brick owns the visual recipes and fixed step artwork.

components.title: OTP Field
components.description: OTP Field is segmented one-time-code entry backed by Atom OTP Field. Atom owns accepted characters, focus movement, paste, masking, completion, validation, reset, and one-value form participation; Brick owns cell recipes and the static Group layout part.

components.title: Pagination
components.description: Pagination navigates a finite, known set of numbered pages with native buttons or real URL destinations.

components.title: Password Toggle Field
components.description: Password Toggle Field is native password entry with an explicitly named visibility action, backed by Atom Password Toggle Field. Atom owns visibility state, Field and Form relationships, reset, submission safety, and native input behavior; Brick owns recipes and default eye artwork.

components.title: Popover
components.description: Popover presents click-open contextual content anchored to a trigger or anchor.

components.title: Progress
components.description: Progress is Brick's linear, read-only task-progress component for known, unknown, and buffered work.

components.title: Progress Circle
components.description: Progress Circle is Brick's compact circular task-progress component for known and unknown work.

components.title: Radio Group
components.description: Radio Group is Brick's finished single-selection control for short visible choice sets. Atom owns selection, keyboard, focus, form, validation, direction, and read-only behavior; Brick owns the circular visual, sizes, layout, states, and stable customization hooks.

components.title: Rating
components.description: Rating is Brick's styled score input and aggregate display. Root and Item expose one accessible Atom-backed slider for choosing a score. Display presents repeated-star aggregate artwork; Summary presents one star beside a visible numeric value.

components.title: Reorderable List
components.description: Reorderable List is Brick's finished manual-order composition, backed by the published `@flowstack-ui/atom@0.23.0` Reorder behavior.

components.title: Scroll Area
components.description: Scroll Area constrains native browser scrolling to explicit axes while keeping content, input, momentum, and platform scrollbar behavior native. It adopts Atom's Root/Viewport behavior and adds finished gutter, visibility, focus, and semantic-color styling.

components.title: Section
components.description: Section owns responsive logical block rhythm for major page and application regions. It renders one native element and adds no paint, inline measure, child arrangement, content anatomy, role, or behavior.

components.title: Segment Group
components.description: Segment Group is Brick's compact single-choice mode control. Atom Radio Group owns semantics and behavior; Brick owns the segmented surface, shared sizes, and moving selected indicator.

components.title: Select
components.description: Select is Brick's finished single-value, select-only choice control. It is built directly on Atom Select: Atom owns values, open state, option registration, keyboard/typeahead, focus, dismissal, positioning, ARIA, native form participation, validation, and reset. Brick owns the complete visual system and default decorative artwork.

components.title: Show
components.description: Show keeps content mounted and adds it to visual layout from one fixed viewport breakpoint. It is CSS responsive visibility, not conditional React rendering. When visible, its host is layout-transparent so parent flex and grid spacing continue to apply directly to its children.

components.title: Sidebar
components.description: Sidebar coordinates a finished persistent complementary panel with main content on Atom Sidebar state and accessibility behavior.

components.title: Skeleton
components.description: Skeleton preserves expected content geometry while an application-owned loading operation is incomplete.

components.title: Skip Link
components.description: Skip Link provides a finished, visible-on-focus bypass link and its matching primary-content destination. Atom owns native anchor behavior, focus transfer, scrolling, target focusability, composition, and refs; Brick owns the overlay presentation and stable customization hooks.

components.title: Slider
components.description: Slider is Brick's styled numeric single-value and range input, backed by Atom 0.19.6. It works alone or as the sole control in `Field`; it is not a grouped choice collection and does not require `Fieldset`.

components.title: Stack
components.description: Stack is Brick's one-dimensional layout primitive. Use VStack for a fixed vertical flow, HStack for a fixed horizontal row, and Stack when the axis changes at a Brick breakpoint. Stack.Item controls how an individual child uses available space.

components.title: Status
components.description: Status presents one compact passive state with a semantic indicator and a visible readable label, or a decorative indicator beside text that already carries the same state.

components.title: Surface
components.description: Surface paints a semantic region with a controlled tone and background level, optional border, elevation, radius, and inset. Ordinary Surface renders one native element. Optional Media, Scrim, and Content parts layer decorative authored media behind foreground content without adding interaction or runtime color context.

components.title: Swipeable Item
components.description: Swipeable Item is a styled three-part boundary that reveals quick actions from logical start or end. Atom owns gesture and keyboard behavior; Brick owns the recipes, surfaces, containment, focus paint, and stable customization hooks.

components.title: Switch
components.description: Switch is Brick's finished binary setting control. Atom owns semantics, state, keyboard, validation, forms, and composition; Brick owns track/thumb visuals, sizes, state paint, motion, and customization hooks.

components.title: Table
components.description: Table presents static row-and-column relationships with native HTML semantics, finished visual recipes, logical alignment, and explicit responsive containment. Atom owns the semantic table primitives and sort metadata; Brick owns presentation.

components.title: Tabs
components.description: Tabs switches between related peer panels while preserving complete keyboard, selection, and panel relationships through Atom.

components.title: Text
components.description: Text is Brick's finished family for authored headings, paragraphs, inline copy, captions, supporting descriptions, and status copy. `Heading`, `Paragraph`, `Caption`, and `Eyebrow` provide common semantic defaults; `Text` keeps the selected HTML element independent from its visual recipe.

components.title: Textarea
components.description: Textarea is Brick's finished native multi-line plain-text control. It composes released Atom value, form, Field, validation, auto-resize, and character-count behavior with Brick's visual recipes and customization hooks.

components.title: Toast
components.description: Toast reports a temporary, non-blocking application outcome or process update. Brick owns its finished viewport, card, glyph, spacing, and responsive recipes; Atom owns the store, queue, timers, announcements, focus, keyboard, portal, swipe, and lifecycle.

components.title: Toggle
components.description: Toggle is a persistent pressed/unpressed command built on Atom Toggle with Brick visual recipes.

components.title: Toggle Group
components.description: ToggleGroup coordinates related single- or multiple-selection pressed commands using Atom state and keyboard behavior plus Brick recipes.

components.title: Toolbar
components.description: Toolbar presents related commands as one named, keyboard-navigable control group.

components.title: Tooltip
components.description: Tooltip supplies a short supplementary label or description for a trigger.

components.title: Tree
components.description: Tree presents a one-dimensional hierarchy with Atom-owned focus, keyboard, selection, expansion, typeahead, direction, form, and accessibility behavior. Brick supplies a finished content row, decorative indicator, recipes, depth, guides, states, motion, and customization hooks.

components.title: Tree Grid
components.description: Tree Grid presents hierarchical rows with Atom-owned cell navigation, expansion, selection, active-cell semantics, and sortable-header activation. Brick supplies finished table paint, hierarchy artwork, recipes, and overflow; applications own records, coordinates, and data transforms.

components.title: Visually Hidden
components.description: Visually Hidden keeps authored text available to assistive technology while removing its visual layout footprint.

components.title: ZStack
components.description: ZStack is Brick's depth-layout primitive. It places authored children in one shared CSS Grid cell so layers overlap without absolute positioning or visual reordering.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.description: Install Brick, load its visual foundation, and compose your first finished interface.

guides.title: Theming
guides.description: Map your visual identity onto Brick's semantic CSS contract without replacing component recipes.

guides.title: Accessibility
guides.description: Brick applies finished visual recipes to the behavior, semantics, and focus contracts supplied by Atom.

guides.title: Composition
guides.description: Build interfaces from explicit component anatomy and application-owned layout without private coupling.
